subject: Intermittent 503 spike affecting payment authorizations — verification & eligibility check
messages:
From: Liz Moreno <liz@falkonpay.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@falkonpay.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s impacting payment auths — need verification and compensation guidance

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a brief but high-impact spike of 503 responses against Redwood's text-generation endpoint that power our payment authorization flow. The first unusual spike started at ~08:44 PST and ended ~08:58 PST (we're attaching a screenshot with a short sample). During that 14-minute window our auth success rate dropped from 99.97% to ~86% and we saw increased latencies for retries.

Concrete ask: can you confirm Redwood's measured error window for our tenant and advise whether this meets the threshold for an SLO breach / service credit? We also need the raw request IDs (examples below) and any relevant ingress/load-balancer metrics and upstream logs to reconcile with our own traces.

Sample request ids from our side: 3b7f1d, 3b7f2a, 3b7f3c.

We realize short blips happen but this one materially affected several high-value transactions. If you can point us at an RCA or provide the logs for our audit that would be helpful.

Attaching: screenshot-503-sample.png (image)

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if it's easier.

Liz Moreno
Director, Platform Engineering
FalkonPay

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Moreno <liz@falkonpay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s impacting payment auths — need verification and compensation guidance

Hi Liz — thanks for the heads-up and for including sample request ids. We're sorry for the disruption. I've opened an internal incident (INC-20280305-NaF) and looped in Vanessa and Priyom to pull the evidence set.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- We'll compute the error-rate and the exact service-side window for your tenant and share candidate boundaries within the hour.
- We'll produce a raw log bundle and LB metrics CSV for reconciliation (format preference: gzipped tar with a top-level manifest is great).
- We'll also flag this to our SLO team for a preliminary eligibility check; formal credit calculations require the final window and error aggregation.

Can you confirm whether you want: (a) the raw logs only, or (b) logs plus pre-filtered entries that match the request ids you provided? We can do either. Also, would you like an emergency call now or later today?

Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>; Liz Moreno <liz@falkonpay.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s impacting payment auths — need verification and compensation guidance

On Mon, Mar 5, 2028 at 9:36 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Liz — thanks for the heads-up and for including sample request ids. We're sorry for the disruption. I've opened an internal incident (INC-20280305-NaF) and looped in Vanessa and Priyom to pull the evidence set.

Folks — preliminary look at prod LB metrics and our error aggregation indicates a clear spike starting at 08:42:19 PST and tailing off by 08:59:07 PST for the cluster that serves FalkonPay traffic. Error-rate during that period exceeded the configured 0.5% SLO threshold for the 5m aggregation window.

I'll attach the raw bundle and LB metrics CSV to this thread once we finish redaction for PII (should be in your preferred gzipped tar format). For now, I'm sharing candidate window and a short summary:
- Candidate service window: 2028-03-05T08:42:19-07:00 to 2028-03-05T08:59:07-07:00
- Peak error-rate (1m): 14.3% at 08:48
- Primary symptom: transient routing mis-association during autoscaling that caused a subset of requests to fall back to a warm-up path returning 503s; tracing indicates increased backend queuing while the autoscaler reconciled node states.

We'll produce:
1) raw-log-bundle-20280305.tar.gz (gzipped, includes manifest.txt)
2) lb-metrics-20280305.csv (load balancer metrics, per-minute)
3) short timeline + mitigation notes (internal PM)

Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Moreno <liz@falkonpay.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 12:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s impacting payment auths — verification & eligibility check

Hi Liz — following up with the assembled artifacts and our read.

Attached / shared:
- raw-log-bundle-20280305.tar.gz (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-log-bundle)
- lb-metrics-20280305.csv
- short timeline and root-cause notes (summary below)

Preliminary determination: based on the candidate window Vanessa called out and the tenant-scoped error aggregation, this meets the terms for an SLO breach for the impacted interval. We will calculate the final credit using the full historical baseline and your contract's credit formula; that typically takes 3–5 business days to finalize the math and produce a credit memo.

Next steps and timeline:
- Day 0 (today): share artifacts and preliminary window (done).
- Day 1–3: SRE/Risk to finalize error aggregation and compute credit amount; you'll receive an estimate and the exact hours/duration used in the computation.
- Day 10 (by): formal postmortem delivered to you with long-term mitigations and rollout plan to avoid recurrence.

If you prefer escalation to account management or want a faster credit turnaround, let me know and I can route to our finance/sales ops team for priority handling.

Thanks again for flagging the request and for the example ids — they helped speed the reconciliation.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
